memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not have sexual relations with a man as one does with a woman; that is detestable. Do not have sexual relations with an animal and defile yourself with it. A woman must not present herself to an animal to have sexual relations with it; that is a perversion.'" - Lev 18:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These verses, along with everything before them in the chapter, point back to a design.

God made humanity male and female, and He established marriage between a husband and a wife as the setting for sexual union (Gen 2:24). Jesus affirmed that pattern when He was asked about marriage, going back past Moses to creation itself (Matt 19:4-6). The New Testament writers continue in the same direction. That has been the consistent understanding of the Christian church across every tradition and every century, and it remains the position of Scripture.

But how we hold this matters as much as what we hold.

Notice where verse 22 sits. It is one item in a long chapter that also condemns adultery, incest and child sacrifice. Scripture does not single it out as uniquely terrible, and neither should we. Paul's lists of sin regularly place sexual sin alongside greed, slander, and pride — and then say to the church: and that is what some of you were. But you were washed (1 Cor 6:11).

Some who read this will be believers who experience same-sex attraction and are seeking to follow Christ faithfully at real cost. If that is you: you are not a category. You are a brother or sister, and the church needs you.

And all of us come to Christ the same way. Not as people who kept the standard, but as people who did not.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you hold Scripture's teaching with humility as well as conviction?
2. Have you treated some sins as worse than others in ways Scripture does not?
3. Is your church a place where anyone can be honest and still be loved?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me hold Your Word faithfully and hold people gently, never using one against the other. Thank You that all of us come to Christ as those who needed washing. Amen.
